disclosures: The continuation request shape (a text block after tool_results) has never been sent to the live API; a refusal cannot be triggered on demand. If the API rejected it, that is a non-transient 400: the harness raises and a --resume hits the same 400.

The budget note can go unseen in one corner: at very large context the stop reserve is near $8.6, so one call jumping from below $32 past about $36 (for example a cache expiry near 900k context) sends the note and stops before another call.

editor_cost_estimate.basis: Measured: the per-call means and the back-test (dry runs 1-2). Judgement, not measurement: the real-run scenarios. The dry runs used a dummy model, so real thinking and tool output are scaled up: 'expected' about 1.7x the dry write and 1.8x the dry output, 'high' about 3.1x and 3.7x (7,500 per call reaches the 900k context stop at turn 120). Forward results stay small in the real run (dry: about 400 chars; arrays go to npz files), so growth comes from run_python stdout (<= 20k chars), the editor's code and its thinking. Expiries are the largest uncertainty: the 1h cache lapses when a tool call plus generation passes 1 h start to start. Measured on the real-model smoke run (n = 1-2 rows, so a sanity check): paired 28.7 s/row, so a largest 48-pair pass with both arms edited takes about 46 min; prefix 8.5 s/row, about 36 min at 256 rows; read 4.5 s/text, about 38 min at 512 texts (the inventory's 6.27 s/text, from more rows, gives about 54 min). A paired pass whose outputs lengthen to 160 tokens (117.8 s/row) still takes about 3.1 h, and a crash resume can add one, so the scenarios keep 3 and 10 expiries: the 48-pair bound removes the forced expiry of a largest pass, and the model has no term for pass size.

launch: cd ~/Code/llm-memctl; the Console workspace limit is $50 and the key is in .env
setsid .venv/bin/python scripts/exp51_harness.py loop --run runs/exp51/editor_run --client api --backend hf --i-have-the-go > runs/exp51/editor_run/loop.log 2>&1 &
the harness writes runs/exp51/editor_run/harness_pid.json; check own_group is true
stop only with scripts/exp51_stop.sh runs/exp51/editor_run (kills the recorded process group; never $! or pgrep)
after a crash: the same command with --resume (no other change)
rules.lost_call: On resume, if the transcript ends on a user record, one call is booked at its worst case (context at the 1h write price + max_tokens at the output price) as a meter placeholder and ledger kind lost_call_placeholder; never trued down.

refusal.rule: An isolated refusal: the refused response is logged and never joins the messages; the fixed text below is appended once as a text block to the user turn that drew it (transcript record user_amend) and the request is sent. Two consecutive refusals (the continuation itself refused) or a third refusal overall: the run ends, documented under D-45; submissions already made stand and go to replay. No fallback model. stop_details is in the transcript only (the ledger is mirrored into the editor's sandbox).

rules.resume: A resume after an infrastructure or harness crash is the same run, not a second editor run (D-45 is not engaged). Messages are rebuilt verbatim from transcript.jsonl (append-only); the ledger and api_usage.json carry the bounds and the meter.
